_meta.indication: Treatment of generalized myasthenia gravis (gMG) in adult patients who are anti-acetylcholine receptor (AChR) antibody positive

pivotal_trials.design: Multicenter, randomized (1:1), double-blind, placebo-controlled, 12-week study of zilucoplan 0.3 mg/kg once-daily subcutaneous injection versus placebo
pivotal_trials.population: Adults with anti-AChR antibody positive generalized myasthenia gravis (gMG)
pivotal_trials.endpoint: Change from baseline in MG-ADL (Myasthenia Gravis-Specific Activities of Daily Living) total score after 12 weeks of treatment
pivotal_trials.result: MG-ADL change from baseline: zilucoplan LS mean -4.39 vs placebo -2.30; LS mean difference -2.09 (95% CI -3.24, -0.95), p<0.001. QMG difference -2.94 (95% CI -4.39, -1.49), p<0.001.

key_safety: Most common adverse reactions (>=10%): injection site reactions (29% vs 16% placebo), upper respiratory tract infections (14% vs 7%), and diarrhea (11% vs 2%). Key serious safety concerns: serious meningococcal infections (class effect), other serious infections, and pancreatitis.
target_moa: Complement C5 inhibitor: binds complement component C5 and inhibits its cleavage to C5a and C5b, thereby inhibiting formation of the membrane attack complex (MAC), which mediates tissue damage at the neuromuscular junction

boxed_warning.content: WARNING: SERIOUS MENINGOCOCCAL INFECTIONS — ZILBRYSQ increases the risk of serious infections caused by Neisseria meningitidis; life-threatening and fatal meningococcal infections have occurred in patients treated with complement inhibitors. Complete/update meningococcal vaccination at least 2 weeks prior to first dose.

rems.type: ZILBRYSQ is available only through a restricted program under a Risk Evaluation and Mitigation Strategy (REMS) called ZILBRYSQ REMS, because of the risk of serious meningococcal infections.

advisory_committee.vote: No advisory committee was convened; the review states 'Not applicable' for the Advisory Committee Summary.

orphan_indication.text: Orphan drug designation granted August 26, 2019 for the treatment of myasthenia gravis

citations.quote: Orphan drug designation was granted on August 26, 2019, for the treatment of myasthenia gravis. With the orphan drug designation, the Applicant was exempt from Pediatric Research Equity Act requirements.

summary.text: ZILBRYSQ (zilucoplan) was reviewed as a standard (non-priority) NDA 216834 and approved based on a single adequate and well-controlled Phase 3 study (MG0010) with confirmatory mechanistic/pharmacodynamic evidence. It had orphan drug designation for myasthenia gravis, which exempted it from PREA pediatric requirements. It was not an accelerated approval.

citations.quote: The Applicant submitted results from a single adequate and well-controlled study (Study MG0010), with confirmatory evidence from pharmacodynamic/mechanistic data, that provide substantial evidence of effectiveness of zilucoplan for the indication which supports approval for the treatment of adults with gMG who are anti-AChR-positive.

requirement.text: 4487-1 Conduct a worldwide descriptive study that collects prospective and retrospective data in women exposed to zilucoplan during pregnancy and/or lactation to assess risk of pregnancy and maternal complications, adverse effects on the developing fetus and neonate, and adverse effects on the infant. Infant outcomes will be assessed through at least the first year of life. The minimum number of patients will be specified in the protocol.

requirement.text: 4487-2 Perform a lactation trial (milk only) in lactating women who have received therapeutic doses of zilucoplan using a validated assay to assess concentrations of zilucoplan in breast milk and the effects on the breastfed infant as applicable.
